steps.text: Combine butter, hot sauce, ketchup, and honey in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes. Use sauce for cooked chicken wings or pieces.

raw_recipe.headline: Scott's Buffalo Wing Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This mild ketchup-based hot sauce made with honey is a little sweet, a little spicy, and a lot delicious when tossed with fried or grilled chicken.
raw_recipe.name: Scott's Buffalo Wing Sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Combine butter, hot sauce, ketchup, and honey in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes. Use sauce for cooked chicken wings or pieces.

review.reviewBody: HELPFUL TIPS THAT MAKE THIS WORK FOR ME: Say NO to BUTTER!!! lol After trying the most popular wings recipes on this site, I got the baking down (350 for 45 min, take out and re-spray w/pam to make crispy, then 375 for 15 min) .........but I was not satisfied w/the hot sauce! No matter what I added or reduced, it still tasted too buttery. I also didn't want hot because we have toddlers in the house who eat them. Well, this recipe was a hit BUT with some minor modifications like NO BUTTER!!! Even when you cut the butter in half, you still can taste it. Plus it makes the sauce slide off the wings. I add about 2T ketchup or a tad more to the 2T honey and 1/3C hot sauce of any kind. The ketchup and honey really cut down on it being hot ...like the butter would but w/o adding the unneeded GREASE! They stick real nicely too! I love them!!! So if you keep thinking something is just not right, try my suggestions!

Used 1/3 cup sriracha and 1/3 cup ketchup with 1/3 cup honey. Turned oven to broil but kept oven rack in the middle. Baked wings for 15 minutes on 1 side, basted with sauce and baked for another 5. Then, turned over, basted and baked for 5 minutes. Basted again and baked for 5 more minutes. Perfect, especially since it was my 1st time making them! Family was impressed!

Here are a few tips from making this sauce so many times. - The sauce tastes best with Franks Redhot sauce, and Heinz ketchup. Make sure not to skip the honey. -The longer you let the sauce simmer, the thicker it will get. - Depending on the brand of butter or margarine you use, sometimes the the oil likes to seperate from the rest of the sauce. In these instances I use a small bat powered milk frother to mix the sauce(a hand immersion blender should work fine also). -If you like a hotter sauce, use equal parts butter, ketchup, and hot sauce.

My son who is allergic to tons of food including peanuts, tree nuts, dairy, egg,seafood saw a picture of chicken wings and wanted to have some “spicy chicken wings”. What’s a mama to do? Go to her trusted all recipes app. This recipe seemed doable and allergen free so I gave it a shot. My son loved it! Although it was a tad spicy on him (it was a first time for him to have anything spicy) he ate it all without me forcing or bribing him. Even my husband approves. He said it felt like eating in a restaurant. The only change I did was to marinate the wings with some lemon, soy sauce and pepper. I feel like the chicken needs to have some flavor seep in and not just outside. I followed the other reviewer on how to cook the wings in the oven.

SOO easy! For the wings, I rinsed and dried them with paper towels. Using a simple mixture of all-purpose flour, salt, pepper and cayanne pepper, I dredged the chicken in the flour mixture then set on a wire rack that I placed on top of a cookie sheet. This way the juices didn't cause the chicken to turn out soggy. Baked the chicken at 400 for about 45 minutes (flipping halfway)...they were perfectly crispy!!! We poured the sauce over the cooked wings and...YUMMMM!!!! They disappeared within minutes!

Doubled this recipe and only added 3 tbsp. Baked frozen wings, pulled them out a little ear, mixed the wings in with the sauce and re cooked for 10 min and then used as a dipping sauce. So good and got lots of compliments. This was also the first time I made wings!
I made this sauce exactly as listed at first. It tasted like spicy tomato soup. My husband agreed. The good thing is that it is very easy to modify - which we did - and ended up with a great sauce.

4 ingredients + personal imagination = 1 great sauce!! Scott's recipe is great as-is for wings. I changed the proportions of the ingredients a little and added chopped garlic when making Buffalo Chicken Sandwiches out of chopped cooked chicken. (1/2 cup each of Frank's and Heinz, 2Tbs butter, healthy Tbs of honey, and one minced garlic clove.) Serve on a bun, or dinner rolls for a fun snack! Thanks Scott -- this one's a winner!

This is a great recipe. I like my wings hot so I used a habanero sauce called Dailey's Habanero sauce found in the produce section at Food Lion. I also used 2 1/2 tbs honey and 2 tbs of brown sugar. I added one minced garlic clove also. I have made this 4 timees in less than a week. I am a wing fanatic and this is my new wing sauce. Finger lickin Lip smackin good. Thanks Scott.

This was great especially for my family as we don't like the hot stuff. I did as another review suggested and leave out most of the butter (cut down to 2tbls) and I doubled the ketchup and honey so I had enought sauce for the amount of wings I had. I would definetly make this again!

We really liked the taste of this sauce so that's why 5 stars but the butter kept separating from the rest of the ingredients. You had to keep stirring it up to keep it blended. Since that first time I only use 2 to 4 tablespoons of butter and it didn't separate as badly.
My new favorite “go to” recipe. Not to spicy. Kids loved it. Hubby loved ‘em. It is a winner. Once you learn basic.. tweet to your own preferences. I did add garlic powder
Absolutely delicious. Perfect spice with a buttery smooth flavour.
My family likes it
Very good.

Delicious!! I loved this sauce and it had a nice thickness to it that coated the wings well. It was something different other than the regular hot sauce and butter buffalo sauce. The only thing I did differently was added more hot sauce, a 1:1 butter to hot sauce ratio, since we like ours spicier, and added a dash of garlic powder. The slight sweetness from the honey and ketchup give it such a nice flavor. Thank you for the recipe! I can see I will be using this sauce very frequently for our buffalo wings!

We liked this a lot. Based on the other reviews, I cut the butter in half and used a half cup of the hot sauce. I could have used even more hot sauce, but it was very good. Other than that I kept it as the recipe called for.
My favorite wing sauce.
This is awful. It tastes like buttery spicy tomato soup. Definitely not what we are looking for our chicken wings.

Very, very similar to what I grew up with in Buffalo. Delicious as is, or if you prefer a suicide wing version you can skip the honey and up the Frank's hot sauce with some cayenne or ghost pepper juice.
